problem: Transformer-based novel view synthesis models like LVSM suffer from quadratic complexity in the number of input views and inefficient parameter sharing across diverse token types.
approach: Efficient-LVSM uses a dual-stream architecture with decoupled co-refinement attention that applies intra-view self-attention for inputs and self-then-cross attention for target views, eliminating unnecessary computation.
contribution: Achieves 29.86 dB PSNR on RealEstate10K with 2.0 dB improvement over LVSM, 2× faster training convergence, and 4.2× faster inference while enabling zero-shot generalization and incremental inference.

problem: Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning significantly underperforms supervised learning on complex datasets because learning discriminative representations is difficult under unreliable supervision from only positive and unlabeled data.
approach: NcPU combines a noisy-pair robust non-contrastive loss (NoiSNCL) that aligns intra-class representations despite unreliable supervision with a phantom label disambiguation scheme providing conservative negative supervision via regret-based label updates.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements over state-of-the-art PU methods across diverse datasets, bridging the 14.26% gap on CIFAR-100, and demonstrates real-world application to post-disaster building damage mapping.

problem: The underlying mechanisms by which RL fine-tuning enhances LLM capabilities beyond supervised fine-tuning remain underexplored across different model families.
approach: The study uses edge attribution patching to compare LLM internals before and after RL fine-tuning, analyzing how online RL post-training reshapes information flow and activation patterns.
contribution: Identifies two robust effects of online RL: increased average activation intensity and greater activation pattern diversity (higher entropy), suggesting RL makes information flow more redundant and flexible; DPO-trained models deviate from these trends.

problem: Vision-Language Models and multimodal models often generate biased outputs including attribute misalignment with input images and reinforcement of harmful stereotypes, and existing debiasing methods degrade performance.
approach: Adaptive Logit Adjustment (ALA) performs post-hoc debiasing by directly adjusting token probabilities during autoregressive generation using external bias classifiers and gradient-based importance analysis to identify bias-inducing tokens.
contribution: Effectively mitigates bias in image captioning and VQA tasks while maintaining contextual accuracy and demonstrates model-agnostic applicability across VLMs and LMMs.

problem: Existing feature attribution methods like Shapley values and LIME are computationally impractical and lack robustness guarantees when applied to random subspace methods used for certified adversarial and backdoor defenses.
approach: EnsembleSHAP provides intrinsically faithful feature attribution by reusing computational byproducts of random subspace methods to achieve computational efficiency while maintaining essential attribution properties.
contribution: First work to establish provable robustness against explanation-preserving attacks on feature attribution for random subspace methods, with comprehensive evaluations against backdoor, adversarial, and jailbreak attacks.

problem: Developing generalizable reasoning capabilities in multimodal large language models remains challenging when trained purely on benchmark-specific data.
approach: Visual Game Learning (ViGaL) uses reinforcement learning on simple arcade-like games (e.g., Snake) as surrogate tasks to develop transferable reasoning skills in a 7B-parameter MLLM.
contribution: The RL-trained model outperforms specialist models on MathVista and MMMU benchmarks without seeing worked solutions or diagrams, while preserving performance on general visual benchmarks.

problem: Machine learning progress on seismic wavefield problems is hindered by ad hoc comparisons, lack of fair reporting, and missing rigorous benchmarks, making it difficult to evaluate and compare different approaches.
approach: The Common Task Framework introduces curated datasets at multiple scales (global, crustal, local) with standardized task-specific metrics for forecasting, reconstruction, and generalization evaluation across various seismic scenarios.
contribution: Provides a structured foundation for rigorous head-to-head algorithm evaluation with hidden test sets, revealing strengths and limitations of methods for reconstructing seismic wavefields from sparse measurements.

problem: LLM computations are deeply entangled after training, resisting modularization which complicates interpretability, auditing, and maintenance.
approach: Jet Expansions uses jet operators generalizing truncated Taylor series to systematically decompose language models into explicit input-to-output computational paths and complementary remainders.
contribution: Reveals super-exponential path structure in transformers with respect to recursive residual depth, grounds the Logit Lens technique, and enables model inspection including toxicity indexing without curated benchmarks.

problem: Bayesian optimization in large unstructured discrete spaces is hindered by the computational cost of maximizing acquisition functions due to absent gradients.
approach: Thompson Sampling via Fine-Tuning (ToSFiT) eliminates acquisition function maximization by directly parameterizing the probability that a candidate yields maximum reward, leveraging and incrementally adapting prompt-conditioned LLMs.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art sample and computational efficiency on FAQ refinement, protein search, and quantum circuit design, with a novel regret bound matching standard Thompson Sampling guarantees.

problem: Generative policy learning with diffusion and flow-matching models captures multimodal distributions but suffers from high inference costs and training instability due to gradient propagation across sampling steps.
approach: Single-Step Completion Policy (SSCP) trains a generative policy with an augmented flow-matching objective to predict direct completion vectors from intermediate flow samples, enabling one-shot action generation.
contribution: Combines expressiveness of generative models with efficiency of unimodal policies, achieving substantial speed gains over diffusion-based baselines across offline, offline-to-online, and online RL settings and extends to goal-conditioned RL.

problem: Current AI safety frameworks treat harmfulness as binary and lack flexibility to handle borderline cases where humans meaningfully disagree on harm judgments.
approach: PluriHarms is a benchmark generating diverse prompts capturing AI harms across two dimensions—harm axis (benign to harmful) and agreement axis (consensus to disagreement)—with 15,000 ratings from 100 annotators enriched with demographic and psychological traits.
contribution: Demonstrates that personalization significantly improves prediction of human harm judgments and reveals that imminent risks, tangible harms, and annotator traits (toxicity experience, education) systematically explain disagreement.

problem: Processing NeRFs with diverse architectures for downstream tasks requires models designed for specific predefined architectures, limiting generalization.
approach: A Graph Meta-Network trained in an unsupervised contrastive learning framework processes weights from diverse NeRF architectures (MLPs, tri-planes, hash tables) to learn an architecture-agnostic latent representation.
contribution: Demonstrates robust performance across 13 NeRF architectures in classification, retrieval, and language tasks, including generalization to architectures unseen during training, matching or exceeding single-architecture methods.

problem: Continual learning in spiking neural networks struggles to balance task-specific selectivity with adaptive resource allocation while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
approach: Randomized Temporal K-Winner-Take-All (RTK-WTA) SNNs integrate trace-dependent neuronal activation with probabilistic top-k selection, dynamically prioritizing neurons based on spatiotemporal relevance while introducing controlled randomness.
contribution: RTK-WTA surpasses deterministic K-WTA by 3.07–5.0% accuracy on splitMNIST and splitCIFAR100, enhancing inter-class margins and robustness through expanded feature space utilization.

problem: Multi-modal large reasoning models can infer sensitive geolocation information from user-generated images despite their privacy implications.
approach: A three-level privacy risk framework and DoxBench dataset (500 real-world images in 6 categories) evaluate geolocation inference in MLRMs; GeoMiner is proposed as a method to demonstrate real-world attack feasibility.
contribution: Most advanced MLRMs/MLLMs outperform non-expert humans in geolocation inference, revealing that models leverage visual clues and internal world knowledge to infer private location without built-in suppression mechanisms.

problem: Conformal prediction applied naively to segmentation model outputs is inefficient because it treats the complex, non-linear segmentation-to-metric pipeline as a black box.
approach: COMPASS performs calibration directly in the model's representation space by perturbing intermediate features along low-dimensional subspaces maximally sensitive to the target metric.
contribution: Produces significantly tighter conformal prediction intervals than traditional baselines on four medical image segmentation tasks for area estimation of skin lesions and anatomical structures while maintaining valid marginal coverage.

problem: Return-conditioned supervised learning in offline RL treats RL as conditional sequence modeling, leading to overreliance on suboptimal past experiences and reduced effectiveness of trajectory synthesis.
approach: Q-Augmented Dual-Feature Fusion Decision Transformer (QDFFDT) adaptively combines global sequence features and local immediate features through a learnable fusion mechanism.
contribution: Outperforms current methods on D4RL benchmarks, establishing new state-of-the-art performance with improved generalization across different tasks without extensive hyperparameter tuning.

problem: Contrastive learning models applied to diverse and unreliable data sources (misaligned text-image pairs) suffer from robustness issues and hallucinations.
approach: Extended Influence Function for Contrastive Loss (ECIF) provides a closed-form approximation for contrastive models that evaluates influence of both positive and negative samples without retraining.
contribution: Advances transparency of CLIP-style models by offering more accurate assessment of data impact and model alignment for data evaluation, misalignment detection, and misprediction trace-back compared to traditional influence functions.

problem: Flow-based image editing models struggle with large-scale shape transformations, often failing to achieve intended shape changes or inadvertently altering non-target regions.
approach: Follow-Your-Shape computes a Trajectory Divergence Map (TDM) by comparing token-wise velocity differences between inversion and denoising paths, guiding a Scheduled KV Injection mechanism for precise editing.
contribution: Achieves superior editability and visual fidelity in large-scale shape replacement tasks; introduces ReShapeBench, a new benchmark with 120 images and enriched prompt pairs for shape-aware editing evaluation.

problem: Evaluation of Text-to-Speech systems is challenging because subjective metrics like MOS are not easily comparable between works, objective metrics lack validation against subjective scores, and modern TTS systems produce near-human-quality speech.
approach: Text to Speech Distribution Score 2 (TTSDS2) is a more robust metric validated against subjective scores across multiple domains and languages with over 11,000 subjective opinion score ratings.
contribution: TTSDS2 achieves Spearman correlation above 0.50 for every domain and subjective score across 16 compared metrics, with resources including a multilingual dataset and a pipeline avoiding data leakage.

problem: It remains unclear whether LLMs can match the conclusions of systematic reviews written by clinical experts when analyzing the same studies.
approach: MedEvidence is a benchmark pairing findings from 100 systematic reviews with their underlying studies to evaluate 24 LLMs including reasoning and medical specialist models across multiple sizes.
contribution: Finds that reasoning does not necessarily improve performance, larger models do not consistently yield gains, and all models show overconfidence and lack scientific skepticism toward low-quality findings unlike human experts.

problem: Time series forecasting struggles to adaptively balance channel-independent and channel-dependent strategies because different channels exhibit varying levels of meaningful inter-channel interactions.
approach: xCPD is a generic plugin that projects multivariate signals into the frequency domain using graph Fourier basis, groups patches by spectral energy into frequency bands, and applies channel-adaptive routing with frequency-specific experts.
contribution: Consistently enhances both accuracy and generalization across benchmarks when integrated into existing channel-independent and channel-dependent models.

problem: A principled explanation for when diverse specialist teams outperform homogeneous teams in multi-agent task allocation is missing.
approach: Theoretical analysis shows that the curvature of reward aggregation operators determines whether heterogeneity increases reward; Heterogeneity Gain Parameter Search (HetGPS) is a gradient-based algorithm optimizing MARL environment parameters.
contribution: Proves that for broad reward families heterogeneity advantage collapses to a convexity test; HetGPS validates theory on different environments and connects theoretical insights to practical MARL reward design.

problem: Current two-stage LLM development (pre-training and post-training) misses an intermediate stage where efficiency and reasoning adaptivity can significantly improve performance.
approach: Reinforcement Mid-Training (RMT) introduces a dynamic token budget mechanism, curriculum-based adaptive sampling from easy-to-hard tokens, and dual training combining RL with next-token prediction.
contribution: Achieves up to 64.91% performance improvement with only 21% of the reasoning length on language modeling, and mid-training checkpoints provide up to 18.76% improvement in subsequent post-training.

problem: Action anticipation in videos is challenging because models tend to overfit to explicit visual cues and lack high-level semantics to infer latent intentions.
approach: Action-Guided Attention (AGA) uses predicted action sequences as queries and keys to guide attention, emphasizing relevant past moments based on upcoming activity and combining with current frame via a gating function.
contribution: Generalizes well from validation to unseen test sets on EPIC-Kitchens-100; post-training analysis reveals action dependencies and counterfactual evidence internalized by the model.

problem: Understanding protein dynamics is essential for elucidating biological function, but molecular dynamics simulations are computationally expensive and limit scalability.
approach: DynaProt is an SE(3)-invariant framework that predicts protein dynamics by casting the problem through multivariate Gaussians, estimating per-residue marginal anisotropy as covariance matrices and joint pairwise dynamic coupling.
contribution: Achieves high accuracy in predicting residue-level flexibility (RMSF) and enables reconstruction of the full covariance matrix for ensemble generation using orders of magnitude fewer parameters than prior methods.

problem: In LLM post-training with RL, high supervised fine-tuning (SFT) scores do not reliably predict subsequent RL gains or scaled-up post-training effectiveness.
approach: Extensive experiments across hundreds of models identify that generalization loss on held-out reasoning examples and Pass@large k performance are stronger proxies for RL outcomes than SFT scores.
contribution: Prediction based on generalization loss and Pass@large k achieves substantially higher precision than SFT score prediction, improving R² and Spearman rank correlation by up to 0.5 (2x) across math benchmarks.

problem: Designing proteins with high affinity and selectivity for arbitrary ligands remains a major challenge in protein engineering.
approach: Pallatom-Ligand is a diffusion model that performs end-to-end generation of ligand-binding proteins at atomic resolution by directly learning the joint distribution of all atoms in protein-ligand complexes.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art in silico success rates in comprehensive benchmarks with programmable control over global protein fold and atomic-level ligand solvent accessibility.

problem: Text summarization methods overlook global document structure, leading to disrupted coherence and weakened downstream performance while LLM-based methods incur substantial resource costs.
approach: GloSA-sum uses topological data analysis to construct semantic-weighted graphs from sentence embeddings where persistent homology identifies core semantics and logical structures preserved in a protection pool.
contribution: Reduces redundancy while preserving semantic and logical integrity, striking a balance between accuracy and efficiency; benefits downstream LLM tasks by shortening contexts while retaining information.

problem: Inference-time control of diffusion models to satisfy new constraints typically relies on heuristic guidance or requires retraining, with prior approaches using Sequential Monte Carlo having limitations.
approach: CREPE (Controlling with REPlica Exchange) is based on replica exchange, an algorithm designed for sampling problems, that generates particles sequentially and maintains high sample diversity.
contribution: Enables online refinement and early termination with competitive performance across temperature annealing, reward tilting, model composition, and classifier-free guidance debiasing tasks.

problem: Applying RL to retrieval-augmented generation benchmarks like multi-hop QA has yielded limited gains compared to supervised or prompting-only baselines.
approach: FrugalRAG is a two-stage finetuning framework that first trains with supervised finetuning on full-exploration, then applies RL to adaptively prune search depth based on question difficulty with frugality-balanced rewards.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art efficiency-accuracy tradeoffs on HotPotQA and BrowseCompPlus, cutting retrieval cost nearly in half with only ~1,000 examples or even 200 on challenging benchmarks.

problem: Multi-view clustering suffers from inability to preserve sample neighborhood structures across views and adaptive utilization of inter-view similarity.
approach: Relationship Alignment for View-aware Multi-view Clustering (RAV) constructs relationship matrices from deep features per view and aligns them with a global matrix; a view-aware adaptive weighting mechanism for label contrastive learning adjusts intensity based on inter-view similarity.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple benchmarks by promoting cluster-level semantic consistency while preserving natural inter-view relationships.

problem: Protein fitness landscape modeling typically uses property-agnostic representations from pretrained protein language models or assumes independent mutational effects, limiting ability to capture higher-order interactions.
approach: RankFlow is a conditional flow framework that refines PLM representations via property-aligned energy functions and learnable embeddings to capture multi-mutation interactions; Rank-Consistent Conditional Flow Loss enforces correct mutant ordering.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art ranking accuracy and stronger out-of-distribution generalization across ProteinGym, PEER, and FLIP benchmarks.

problem: Large time series models struggle to address variety and nonstationarity of time series, resulting in unsatisfying balance between forecasting performance and generalizability across domains.
approach: Time-Series Adaptive Transformation Optimization (TATO) enables frozen pre-trained LTMs to fit downstream domains through empirically optimal transformation pipelines combining context slicing, scale normalization, and outlier correction.
contribution: Achieves maximum MSE reduction of 68.4% and average decrease of 16.0%, typically optimizing transformation pipelines in under 2 minutes.

problem: Transferring LLM capabilities to super-tiny function calling models is plagued by overfitting, training instability, ineffective binary rewards for multi-solution tasks, and difficulty synergizing techniques.
approach: STAR (Similarity-guided Teacher-Assisted Refinement) introduces Constrained Knowledge Distillation (CKD) augmenting top-k KL to suppress confidently incorrect predictions and Similarity-guided RL providing fine-grained similarity-based rewards.
contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art performance in size classes; a 0.6B STAR model achieves best performance among all open models under certain settings.

problem: Multimodal learning in computational pathology relies on vision and language which lack molecular specificity and provide limited pathological supervision, creating representational bottlenecks.
approach: STAMP (Spatial Transcriptomics-Augmented Multimodal Pathology) integrates spatially-resolved gene expression profiles for molecule-guided joint embedding of pathology images and transcriptomic data using hierarchical multi-scale contrastive alignment.
contribution: Consistently achieves strong performance across six datasets and four downstream tasks; SpaVis-6M is the largest Visium-based spatial transcriptomics dataset to date.

problem: Inverse reinforcement learning methods yield black-box reward models that are difficult to interpret and debug.
approach: GRACE uses large language models within evolutionary search to reverse-engineer an interpretable, code-based reward function directly from expert trajectories that is executable and verifiable.
contribution: Efficiently learns highly accurate rewards on MuJoCo, BabyAI, and AndroidWorld benchmarks with strong policy performance compared to competitive imitation learning and RL approaches.

problem: When generalist robot policies are finetuned on limited demonstrations of new tasks, they overfit to specific demonstrations, losing both prior generalist abilities and within-task generalization.
approach: Parameter merging interpolates weights of finetuned and pretrained models to preserve generalization capabilities of the generalist policy during finetuning.
contribution: Across extensive simulated and real-world experiments, model merging produces a single model inheriting generalist abilities while robustly learning new tasks, outperforming both pretrained and finetuned models on out-of-distribution variations.

problem: Mid-training stages for LLM RL post-training should both learn strong policy priors and enable fast learning through online interactions, but the principles for achieving this remain unclear.
approach: Reasoning as Action Abstractions (RA3) introduces temporal abstractions via a temporal variational bound, iteratively discovering temporally-consistent latent structures via RL and fine-tuning on bootstrapped data.
contribution: Improves average performance on HumanEval and MBPP by 8 and 4 points over base model; achieves faster convergence and higher asymptotic performance on HumanEval+, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench, and Codeforces.

problem: Most adversarial sample research focuses on constrained perturbations that do not accurately reflect test-time errors encountered in real-world settings.
approach: NatADiff uses denoising diffusion guided by time-travel sampling and augmented classifier guidance to generate natural adversarial samples by guiding trajectories toward the intersection of true and adversarial classes.
contribution: Achieves comparable white-box attack success rates to state-of-the-art while exhibiting significantly higher transferability across models and improved alignment with natural test-time errors.

problem: Diffusion Transformers have substantial computational overhead due to iterative denoising and deep transformer blocks, limiting accessibility and practical deployment of high-quality video generation.
approach: ScalingCache exploits inherent redundancy in model representations through lightweight offline analysis and dynamic reuse of previously computed activations during inference at certain denoising steps.
contribution: Achieves approximately 2.5× acceleration on Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo with only 0.5% drop in VBench scores, and 3.1× near-lossless acceleration on FLUX with human preference tests showing comparable quality.
